content:
Key observations:
- Soybean leaves with interveinal necrosis: tissue between veins is dead/brown while major veins remain green
- Large chlorotic and necrotic blotches confined between veins
- Midvein and lateral veins remain green
- Affects multiple leaves across the canopy
- No pustules, no white mold, no powdery coating, no angular water-soaked lesions

This pattern — interveinal chlorosis and necrosis with veins staying green — is the hallmark of Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS). The large irregular blotches between veins with the veins remaining green is diagnostic. Brown Stem Rot can look similar but typically shows more uniform browning; SDS produces this distinct interveinal pattern. The symptoms match SDS precisely.
